---
title: "Save, sync and stop"
---

Saving a notebook and saving your work to GitHub are **not the same operation**.

This distinction is important.

| Operation | What it does | Where the work exists |
|---|---|---|
| **Save** | Writes the current file in the Codespace | Remote Codespace disk |
| **Commit** | Records a named snapshot of repository changes | Git history inside the Codespace |
| **Sync Changes** | Sends your commits to GitHub | Your permanent GitHub repository |

Your GitHub repository is the safety copy that should survive beyond the
lifetime of an individual Codespace.

## Save your files

Save notebooks and other edited files normally with **File → Save** or
`Ctrl+S` (`Cmd+S` on macOS).

A saved file is safe when a Codespace is merely stopped and restarted, but it
has not yet been transferred to your GitHub repository.

## Commit your work

Open **Source Control** using the branch-shaped icon in the left activity bar.

You will see the files that have changed.

1. Stage the relevant files using the **+** button. Staging simply means
   selecting which changed files will be included in the next Git snapshot.
2. Enter a short but meaningful commit message, for example:

   ```text
   Complete Lab 1 symmetry analysis
   ```

3. Select **Commit**.

For routine laboratory work it is acceptable to stage all files that belong to
the current activity.

::: {.callout-warning}
## If you see "Publish Branch"

Your personal workspace should already be connected to a GitHub repository.

If Source Control asks you to **Publish Branch** instead of allowing you to
synchronize normally, you may have opened a Codespace directly from the
template rather than from your personal repository. Stop and ask the instructor
before continuing.
:::

## Synchronize with GitHub

After committing, select **Sync Changes**.

If GitHub asks you to confirm the synchronization, accept the operation.

Then open your repository on GitHub in a normal browser tab and verify that your
latest notebook or file is visible there.

This simple check is especially useful during the first laboratory.

## Stop the Codespace

::: {.callout-important}
## Closing the browser tab does not stop the Codespace

Always stop the Codespace explicitly when you finish working.
:::

The most reliable method is:

1. open <https://github.com/codespaces>;
2. locate your Mineral Science Codespace;
3. select the **...** menu;
4. select **Stop codespace**.

You can also stop it from inside Visual Studio Code:

1. press `Ctrl+Shift+P` on Windows/Linux or `Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS;
2. search for **Codespaces: Stop Current Codespace**;
3. select the command.

Stopping a Codespace ends the running virtual machine while preserving saved
files for the next session. It also avoids unnecessary compute usage.

Do **not** delete your Codespace as part of the normal workflow. Delete it only
when explicitly instructed or when you are certain that all required work has
already been synchronized to GitHub.

## End-of-session routine

Use the same sequence every time:

```text
SAVE
  ↓
COMMIT
  ↓
SYNC CHANGES
  ↓
VERIFY ON GITHUB
  ↓
STOP CODESPACE
```
